C11.v: •  ONE route dominates ~all commercial LFP tonnage: high-temperature solid-state CARBOTHERMAL REDUCTION fed by a (co-precipitated) FePO4 precursor  ->  spray-dried with Li source + carbon  ->  calcined under inert gas. These are linked STAGES of one workflow, not competing methods.

C12.v: •  The only other route at meaningful commercial tonnage is Shenzhen Dynanonic's proprietary LIQUID-PHASE process (SELPS, auto-thermal evaporative; patent US20140239235A1).

C13.v: •  HYDROTHERMAL is a smaller/legacy commercial route (historically Sud-Chemie; today premium LMFP e.g. Taiheiyo 'Nanolitia'). Everything else is lab-scale, with melt-casting and spray pyrolysis demonstrated at pilot.

C14.v: •  China makes ~95-98% of global LFP CAM. 2024 leader: Hunan Yuneng (~28.8% share); 2025 Yuneng shipments >1 Mt. LMFP is ramping, led by Hengchuang Nano + Ronbay.

C15.v: •  Correction to a common assumption: Aleees (Taiwan) uses an in-house iron-phosphate PRECURSOR route (+ solid-state), NOT hydrothermal.

C16.v: •  Western/Indian production became possible largely after key foundational LFP patents expired (~2022-2023). Many Western projects are announced/pre-production and volatile (e.g. ICL's US plant was cancelled in Nov 2025).

C6.v: Precursors melted to an ingot, then crushed

C7.v: Reaction in a liquid medium (aqueous / organic / ionic liquid)

D8.v: Spray pyrolysis; spray drying (+ calcination); ultrasonic spray; flame spray

E8.v: Spray DRYING is a standard commercial granulation step. Spray pyrolysis is lab/pilot.

C9.v: Combine/modify the above, or use exotic energy

D9.v: Template-assisted; microwave-hydrothermal; electrospinning; plasma (incl. 6K UniMelt); One-Pot (Nano One)

E9.v: Mostly lab. Emerging pilots: Nano One One-Pot; 6K plasma (plant under construction).

B11.v: Bottom line: the commercial LFP workflow is a CHAIN across categories -> C (precipitate FePO4 precursor) -> D (spray-dry with Li + carbon) -> A (carbothermal solid-state calcination). For LMFP, the workhorse is co-precipitation of a Mn-Fe precursor -> spray-dry -> solid-state calcination.
